stage_2_story.text_en:
Moshe's granddaughter Shira had been training seriously for athletics for two years. One Sunday morning, she invited Grandpa Moshe to come and watch her practice session at the local track.

Moshe sat on the bench as Shira's coach, a tall woman named Tamar, put the group through their workout. First came a conditioning session — exercises to build the body's base strength before moving to the track itself.

Then Tamar set up a circuit with four stations around the field. Shira moved from one to the next without stopping, which impressed Moshe greatly. 'How does she do it?' he whispered to himself.

Afterwards, Tamar explained: 'Shira has excellent endurance. Most athletes her age cannot hold their technique when they are tired. But Shira keeps her form even when her stamina is tested.'

She went on: 'We do a lot of interval training. Thirty seconds hard, sixty seconds easy. It builds her performance over time. And she is making great progress — her times have improved every month.'

Moshe watched as Shira finished her last interval run. She walked over, breathing hard but smiling. 'Grandpa, did you see? I hit my target today — one minute and fifty-eight seconds for the four hundred metres!'

Moshe hugged her. 'I saw everything, motek. I did not understand all of it — but I understood one thing. You work very, very hard.'
